title: When {name} asks first, and how to change what it asks
description: What {name} does by itself, what it asks you before doing, what it never does, and how to change each in Settings › Approvals.
answer: {name} reads and makes its own files by itself. Before it uses the internet, moves, deletes or sends anything, it shows you what it will do, and waits. Passwords and payments: never. You choose for each kind of action in {settings} › {approvals}.
tour.here: This is {settings} › {approvals}. Next time, {settings} is in your menu at the foot of the task list.
pane.title: A request to send an email, answered in {name}

demo.answer: Sent to the team, with the minutes attached.
parts: Under {allow}: reading files, making and changing its own, searching, and running calculations on its computer, which is in a sandbox, never yours.

Under {ask}: using the internet, moving and renaming, deleting files, and sending and sharing. A card shows what it is about to do, and {name} waits for your answer: {once}, {always}, {notnow} or {nothing}.
Under {never}: typing passwords and paying. {name} tells you it can’t, and why.
steps.title: Change what {name} asks first
steps: Open {settings}, from your menu at the foot of the task list, then {approvals}.
Each kind of action sits under {allow}, {ask} or {never}. Press one to open its page, and choose where it goes.
A dot marks each kind you changed, and {reset} puts them all back.
show.card: The card, as a task shows it: nothing is sent until you press {once} or {always}.
show.rules: {approvals}: each kind of action is a button under its rule.
good: Answering {always} or {nothing} on a card makes a rule for that kind of action, and {name} says where to take it back.
Once a service is connected, such as your email, its page has rules of its own: reading and searching apart from writing, sending and changing.
In a child’s profile, the parent’s rules hold. When {name} asks, the child can allow it once or say not now, never always.
At work, your organisation may set some rules. They show a lock, and can’t be changed here.
fixes: Answer {always} on its card, or put its kind under {allow} in {approvals}.
Its kind is under {never}, or your organisation keeps it there. Move it in {approvals}, if it has no lock.
